Thought: In nucleophilic acyl substitution reactions, the reactivity of compounds generally depends on the leaving group ability and the stability of the intermediate formed. Carboxylic acid derivatives can be ordered in terms of reactivity from least to most reactive as follows: amides < esters < anhydrides. Anhydrides are the most reactive due to the resonance stabilization of the leaving group, esters are less reactive due to poorer leaving groups, and amides are the least reactive due to strong resonance stabilization of the amide bond. I will now identify these functional groups in the given SMILES strings and order them accordingly.

1. N[C@@H](C(C)C)C(N[C@H](CO)CC1=CC=CC=C1)=O represents an amide.
2. O=C(OC(C)C)CC1=CC=CC=C1 represents an ester.
3. O=C1C=CC(O1)=O represents an anhydride.

Thus, the order from least to most reactive in nucleophilic acyl substitution should be amide < ester < anhydride.
